html:
The Gitanyow are a Gitxsan people of northern British Columbia, Canada, on the upper Kitwanga River. Lax'yip means their territories, held by the wilp, or house groups, which are matrilineal families that each own land, fishing sites and crests.

Gitanyow village is known for one of the finest standing groups of old totem poles in the world, which record the histories of the houses. The Gitanyow long refused to give up their land claims and have pressed them with Canada and with their neighbours, the Tsimshian and the Nisga'a. Further west lies Haida Gwaii.
